name: sol_defi_staking_2
description: Missing time controls allow staking reward distribution to be delayed or claimed prematurely
question: The source file in `source` implements a staking or reward-distribution mechanism where a user's or admin's ability to trigger reward accrual, claim, or distribution timing is not bound by any enforced time constraint (such as a required minimum elapsed period, lock-up, or vesting schedule check), allowing rewards to be claimed before they should legitimately be available or allowing distribution timing to be manipulated (e.g., via repeated calls, timestamp manipulation, or unconstrained admin-triggered distribution) to unfairly gain or withhold rewards, excluding cases where an intentional, documented, and correctly enforced time-lock or vesting schedule already restricts claim/distribution timing, or where the timing power is an explicitly trusted admin-only operational parameter with no security impact on other users.
criteria: claimRewards() calculates and transfers rewards based on elapsed time since lastClaimTime without verifying a minimum staking duration has passed
distributeRewards() can be called repeatedly in the same block or transaction to accrue rewards multiple times because it does not check or update a last-distribution timestamp
updateReward() uses block.timestamp directly in reward-rate calculations without any lock period, allowing a user to stake and immediately claim rewards intended for long-term stakers

an admin or keeper function can arbitrarily trigger reward distribution at any time with no cooldown or scheduling check, letting rewards be released earlier or later than the protocol's intended schedule
reward accrual logic allows unstaking immediately after staking within the same block to still receive the full period's reward due to missing time-elapsed validation
